title: Wren and the Summit
premise: Jude Reyes, a storm chaser drowning in debt to the Vane Syndicate, is hired by her old rival Marisol Quade for an expedition up the Serrano River to its forbidden source, where a storm has raged unbroken for decades and where Jude's missing mentor left behind the truth about the compass she carries. The source turns out to be a machine built by the river towns' founders to hoard memory itself, feeding on belonging while erasing it from everyone downstream. When Marisol reveals she intends to seize the machine's power rather than destroy it, Jude must choose between paying off her debt with complicity or burning her last chance at safety. In the end, Jude shatters the compass into the machine's core, releasing the stolen memories in a single catastrophic storm that washes the debt, the syndicate, and her invisibility away forever.
about_author: Petra Eastwick is a former river guide who spent six seasons mapping headwaters across three continents before turning to fiction. She writes adventure stories about people who run toward weather instead of away from it.

chapters.title: The Debt Collector's Weather
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Chasing a supercell across the plains to earn syndicate money, Jude loses the footage when her rival Marisol Quade appears with a better offer: lead a crew up the Serrano River to its forbidden source. The chapter establishes her debts, her dead mentor's compass, and her instinct to stay invisible. Emotional beat: restless dread, the sense that running has stopped working.

chapters.title: Upstream of Every Map
chapters.summary: Jude's POV, with interludes from crew member Teo's journal. The crew fights rapids, abandoned checkpoints, and towns whose residents can't remember their own names. Jude realizes the compass points not north but toward the source, and that her mentor vanished following this same pull. Emotional beat: growing wonder curdling into unease as belonging looks more like theft.

chapters.title: What the Machine Remembers
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. At the source, they find the Memory Engine: a humming vault holding every memory the river towns surrendered, including Jude's own childhood, which she thought was simply lost. Marisol reveals she plans to claim the machine for the syndicate, making herself the keeper of everyone's pasts. Emotional beat: betrayal and recognition, as Jude sees power's corruption wearing a familiar face.

chapters.title: The Breaking of the Needle
chapters.summary: Jude's POV, closing with Teo's journal. Jude sabotages the engine by driving her shattered compass into its core, unleashing decades of stored memory as a storm that drowns the syndicate's claim and returns the towns their names. She surfaces downstream with no debt, no rival, and no anonymity left. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into belonging; visibility chosen at last.
